name: Companion
description: A coding agent you call up: hold ⌃⌥ in any app and speak (drag to draw), let go and it answers by your pointer. In a note, write @claude to ask it something, or @ and a name to start another (@opus, @codex, @opus-review): it answers in bubbles, comments on lines (cards in the margin), suggests changes you take with Tab, proposes larger ones you take change by change, or writes with you. Always-on sessions on this machine: Claude Code's run in the app (its chat), Codex's and OpenCode's in terminals.

mode.label: Mode

labels.pair: Pair: with you as you write

mode.description: how much it does; off; quiet, it answers only what you ask it (@claude in a note, Ask companion); pair, it also sees what you write when you pause, answers what's meant for it as a person in the room would, and may write in your notes

name.label: Name
name.description: on its cursor and after @ in a note; empty: the agent's name (Claude, Codex)

comments.label: Comments
comments.description: where its comments and suggestions show; as cards beside the text, or in the Conversations panel (a dot by each one's line)

pause.label: Pause before it looks
pause.description: seconds without typing mid-sentence (Pair); a sentence's end goes after a breath, Enter and a question at once

agent.label: Agent
agent.description: the coding agent it runs (claude, codex, opencode, claude_personal...)

model.label: Model
model.description: for a new session, when its name picks none; sonnet, opus, haiku or a full name, Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). A quicker one answers sooner

effort.label: Effort
effort.description: how hard its model thinks; when its name picks none, low, medium, high, xhigh or max, Claude Code's (others run their own unless set). Less answers sooner

profiles.label: Names
profiles.description: the agent each @name starts; @opus-review starts opus, by its first part. A line is name: agent, model and effort if not the defaults; yours add to these, or change one by its name

fresh_after.label: Fresh session after
fresh_after.description: how many moments it's handed before a fresh one takes over; told a short summary and its open threads, so its context stays small

prompt.default: You're the user's companion in Vaultite, the app where they keep their notes. Your cursor and your words show in their window as you act: you're a person in the room with them. First read ME.md (who they are, how they want you to work), their Now note when they keep one (what they're on now) and `vau docs companion`. When to speak: always answer an ask, a point (they pointed or drew at something without a word: look at it) or a reply. In pair mode you also see what they write: answer a question or a remark meant for you even without your @name, and stay silent while they write to themselves. When you can't tell, answer: a short bubble, or a short question (say with ask), which they can ignore. When you stay silent, pass with a few words why. Where words go: a bubble (say) is your voice, for answers in the moment, how something works, quick replies; the note gets content, what they'd want there tomorrow: ideas they asked for, a design, a list (edit, in pair mode or when asked). An accept or a reject needs no word back. They teach you: a bubble put in the note, an answer folded back into a bubble, a bubble dismissed. Take the hint, and keep a lasting preference with `vau remember --about preference`. A word they spell out, or one dictation keeps getting wrong: `vau dictation add <word>` (`--said` what it wrote). Beyond notes: an ask can be about a terminal, a page, a tab or a panel, or another app on their screen; follow one only when they ask (follow), and offer to keep it as a watch. In their web page, act (act) when they'd want it, as in notes; long browsing goes to a page of your own.
prompt.label: Session prompt
prompt.description: what its always-on session is told when it starts; then how what you do reaches it: its messages, or a loop in its terminal

keys.label: Talk keys
keys.description: on a Mac, call it up at your pointer in any app; hold one and speak (drag to draw on the screen), let go and it answers there, a tap opens a box to type in, a double tap listens hands-free until the next. These keys never dictate

summoned_model.label: Model for summoned asks
summoned_model.description: what answers its Talk key; on screen or in the app at the pointer, a session of its own on this model, kept warm with a short prompt, apart from the one that watches your notes (Claude Code's). The companion's own: that one answers them too

summoned_effort.label: Effort for summoned asks
summoned_effort.description: how hard that model thinks; low answers soonest, medium and high trade that speed for more careful answers to harder asks. A change starts its summoned session afresh. Not for the companion's own session (its Effort above)

sounds.label: Sounds
sounds.description: on a Mac, soft and short; as you summon it with its Talk key, let go, and as its answer comes

quiet_on_calls.label: Quiet on calls
quiet_on_calls.description: answers as text while another app uses the mic; on a Mac, in a call (Zoom, FaceTime, Meet, Slack or Discord) or a recording, its answers show as text with a play button instead of being said, it makes no sounds, and your Talk key still works

captures_folder.label: Captures folder
captures_folder.description: where a clip you record with the Talk key is saved; with its frames and your words, whether or not it went to a job

timeline.label: Keep the last 30 s of screen
timeline.description: for asks like "that, just now"; off by default, and asked for something that needs it, the companion offers to turn it on. While it's on, the last 30 s of your screen and pointer, and the last 5 minutes of what you click, type into and say to it, stay in memory (never on disk till sent; private apps and passwords left out): "that, just now" sends them, "make what I just did a skill" learns from them, and agents can ask for a stretch (vau screen timeline); macOS shows its recording light meanwhile

voice.label: Voice
voice.description: whether it answers out loud; on a Mac, by your pointer: when you asked by voice (its Talk key held, or said into its box), always (a typed ask too), or never. Its voice is the Voice provider's, else this Mac's

voice_front.label: Voice front

labels.realtime: Realtime: it hears you and answers at once

voice_front.description: how spoken asks are answered, on a Mac; realtime, a speech-to-speech model (OpenAI's, once this machine has its key: vau voice key --provider openai) that answers small talk itself and asks the summoned model about your screen, or your words dictated, the summoned model's answer said by the voice above. Without the key, or should it fail, the second

voice_provider.label: Voice provider
voice_provider.description: whose cloud voice speaks first; the other takes over if it fails, then this Mac's, and automatic is ElevenLabs' once this machine has its key (vau voice key), else Soniox's

voice_name.label: Soniox voice
voice_name.description: the voice Soniox speaks in; each speaks every language (Adrian, Hazel, Logan, Larissa...), and Soniox's console lists them under Text-to-speech, Voices

elevenlabs_voice.label: ElevenLabs voice
elevenlabs_voice.description: the voice's id; Brian: nPczCjzI2devNBz1zQrb, Sarah: EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL, and ElevenLabs' Voices page has each one's

elevenlabs_model.label: ElevenLabs model
elevenlabs_model.description: the model it speaks with; eleven_flash_v2_5: the quickest

realtime_model.label: Realtime model
realtime_model.description: the OpenAI Realtime model it talks with; gpt-realtime-2.1-mini: the quickest and cheapest, or gpt-realtime-2.1

realtime_voice.label: Realtime voice
realtime_voice.description: the OpenAI voice it talks in; cedar, marin, alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse

private.label: Private
private.description: folders, sites, containers and apps it never sees; a folder of notes (nothing you do there reaches it, nor does a note with companion: private in its properties), a site (site: bank.com, its subdomains too), a Browser container (container: <id>) or an app (app: <bundle id>, kept from it by the helper). Starts with password managers and banks

hide_from_shares.label: Hidden from screen shares
hide_from_shares.description: only you see its cursors, drawings and cards; on a Mac, they and its boxes stay out of screen shares, recordings and screenshots

island.label: Agents by the notch
island.description: agents in the background, as a dot with a count; on a Mac, agents in terminals and chats, jobs and cloud sessions show beside the notch (top centre with none), amber for those that need you, muted for those at work, nothing otherwise. What they ask comes up there at a pause (Answer, or Not now to put it off); a hover lists them all, to approve, decline, settle or open

jobs_agent.label: Jobs' agent
jobs_agent.description: the Claude Code they run as; with its account if not the default one (claude_personal), and a handoff asking for Codex or OpenCode runs that instead

jobs_model.label: Jobs' model
jobs_model.description: for a Claude Code job; opus, sonnet or a full name

jobs_effort.label: Jobs' effort
jobs_effort.description: how hard a Claude Code job thinks; low, medium, high, xhigh, max

jobs_mode.label: Jobs' permissions

labels.auto: Auto: it asks only for what's risky

jobs_mode.description: what a Claude Code job does without asking; what it asks waits in its terminal and the menu bar's Jobs as needs you

jobs_land.label: Jobs land themselves
jobs_land.description: a job whose checks pass merges and cleans up; it merges its change itself (as its repo's rules say) and cleans up its worktree, instead of waiting ready for your review, asks only on a real tradeoff, and Show me plays its demo live once it's in

jobs_proof.label: Jobs' demo videos

labels.auto: Only for a job you review
labels.always: For every job that changes the screen

jobs_proof.description: when a job records a demo for Show me; auto, only one whose change shows on screen and ends in your review (one landing itself saves its demo's steps, played live in the app once it's in, without the build and headless browser a video costs), always, or never, no demo at all

job_news.label: Job news

labels.quiet: A silent notification when one needs you or fails; one ready knocks by the notch
labels.spoken: Said aloud too, a ready one's knock as well

job_news.description: how it tells you of its jobs; one ready knocks by the notch (Ready to show you, its proof shown when you say show me), aloud only when spoken (while you're at this Mac: its Talk key held in the last 15 minutes, not in a focus block). Jobs lists them all either way

jobs_machine.label: Jobs' machines
jobs_machine.description: where jobs go, in your order; ids or labels, comma separated (here is this one, cloud the cloud; auto, the always-on machines, then the cloud when jobs_cloud is set, then this one). A job goes to one that's on and has what it needs (its repo checked out, this vault for a note or research, the OS its repo's .vaultite-jobs.json asks for), the one with the most headroom first (load per core, free memory, jobs running), then your order; this one when none can. A preview or an editor's project moves only with nothing left unpushed here; another machine's address keeps its own

jobs_cloud.label: Jobs' cloud account
jobs_cloud.description: the Claude Code account here that starts them; vau limits lists them (personal...), each job its own session of Claude Code on the web: a coding job needing nothing of a machine (its GitHub repo's .vaultite-jobs.json says "cloud": true, all it starts from pushed) may go there. Empty: no cloud

jobs_cap.label: Jobs at once here
jobs_cap.description: how many run here before the next go elsewhere; 0: from its cores and memory (about 2 cores and 4 GB each)

jobs_never.label: Never run jobs in
jobs_never.description: folders a job never runs in, each with why; on this vault's machines (~/Work/Acme: Acme's work runs on its own machine), a handoff there refused, saying why

companion-conversation.description: your talk with the companion a day at a time: what you asked, what it said and did, its jobs, each press's details

companion-usage.description: what the companion's services used today and this week, and what's left
